skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automates remote Playwright sessions through inference.sh for navigation, element interaction, form workflows, extraction, screenshots, video, proxies, and page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Drive reproducible browser workflows through inference.sh using element references and session-aware commands.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, fenced shell examples, placeholder URLs, relative links, and /dev/null redirection. Confirmed risks include external installation, remote image loading, TOTP exposure through process arguments, and remote screen capture. Credential submission, cookie extraction, local file upload, and page JavaScript require explicit consent and strict scoping.

remediation.issue: Authentication examples transmit secrets through a remote browser service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before authentication, recommend disposable test accounts, and state clearly that credentials and TOTP values cross the inference.sh boundary.

remediation.issue: The guide extracts and prints session cookies.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the cookie logging example, redact sensitive values, and prevent cookies or tokens from entering command output and retained logs.

remediation.issue: File upload and page JavaScript can disclose data or perform broad actions.
remediation.suggestion: Add domain and path allowlists, show the exact target and file before upload, and require confirmation before JavaScript execution.

remediation.issue: Screenshots, videos, and remote assets create privacy and integrity exposure.
remediation.suggestion: Disable recording by default, warn before capturing authenticated pages, redact sensitive fields, and replace mutable remote assets with reviewed local copies.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs users to install an external CLI skill with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the dependency to a reviewed version or commit and document its publisher, permissions, and integrity verification steps.

1. **Open** - Navigate to URL, get `@e` refs for elements
| `open` | Navigate to URL, configure browser (viewport, proxy, video recording) |
| `snapshot` | Re-fetch page state with `@e` refs after DOM changes |
| `interact` | Perform actions using `@e` refs (click, fill, drag, upload, etc.) |
| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |
| `execute` | Run JavaScript code on the page |
| `close` | Close session, returns video if recording was enabled |

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser workflows are slow and difficult to reproduce. This skill drives remote Playwright sessions for navigation, interaction, extraction, screenshots, and video.
actual_capabilities: Opens remote browser sessions with viewport, user agent, proxy, and recording options.
Returns page snapshots with element references for repeatable interactions.
Clicks, fills, types, selects, uploads, drags, scrolls, waits, and navigates.
Captures viewport screenshots, full-page screenshots, and optional session video.
Executes page JavaScript and extracts text, links, metadata, and element details.
Provides shell templates for authentication, form submission, and content capture.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, an account, network access, and the agent-browser service.
Element references expire after navigation or dynamic page changes.
Remote sessions may expose page content, credentials, files, screenshots, and video to external infrastructure.
Website terms, authentication controls, anti-bot measures, and local laws still apply.

use_cases.title: Inspect Web Interfaces
use_cases.description: Open a page, identify interactive elements, and capture current state before making changes.

use_cases.title: Collect Public Page Data
use_cases.description: Extract visible text, links, titles, and screenshots from approved public websites.

use_cases.title: Automate Repeated Form Workflows
use_cases.description: Fill and verify approved forms with controlled inputs and confirmation before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], return the page title and interactive elements, then stop without clicking or entering data.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Public Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], extract the main visible text and links, take a full-page screenshot, then close the session.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Form Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [FORM URL], map fields to my provided values, fill them, and ask for confirmation before submitting.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Scoped Browser Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [PROXY] to inspect [URL], perform only [ALLOWED ACTIONS], record video, extract [FIELDS], and close every session.

output_examples.input: Inspect the contact page and list available form controls without changing anything.
output: Available controls: name, email, message, consent checkbox, and submit button.
No fields were changed and the session was closed.

output_examples.input: Capture the public article page and summarize its visible content.
output_examples.output: The page contains one article, five section headings, twelve links, and a full-page screenshot. The session is closed.

output_examples.input: Fill the approved test form and pause before submission.
output_examples.output: The requested fields are filled. Submission is paused until explicit confirmation is provided.

best_practices: Use approved domains, disposable test accounts, and the minimum required permissions.
Refresh element references after navigation, form submission, or dynamic content changes.
Confirm before uploads, submissions, authentication, recording, or JavaScript execution.
anti_patterns: Do not capture credentials, payment data, private messages, or confidential pages without authorization.
Do not reuse stale element references after the page changes.
Do not leave sessions open or store cookies, screenshots, videos, and extracted data indefinitely.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The inference.sh CLI and its agent-browser service are required. Authentication and network access are also necessary.

faq.question: Does this skill run a local browser?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow sends commands to agent-browser through inference.sh.

faq.question: Why do element references stop working?
faq.answer: Navigation and dynamic page changes invalidate references. Request a new snapshot before continuing.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but credentials and page data may cross a remote service boundary. Use approved test accounts and explicit consent.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Confirm the exact file and destination first, and restrict uploads to approved paths and domains.

faq.question: How should sessions be closed?
faq.answer: Call the close function after every workflow. Closing also returns recorded video when recording is enabled.
